pr_title: Add support for variable output latency in WASAPI audio driver
pr_body:
Fixed the audio 'output latency' project setting not appearing when using the WASAPI audio driver (see [#30562](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/30562)). Added variable output latency support to the WASAPI audio driver for systems that support it.

*Bugsquad edit: This closes #30562.*

Yeah, this is difficult to test. `AudioDriverPulseAudio::get_latency()` seems to be using `pa_stream_get_latency` for this - could it be possible it's returning the stream round trip latency instead of the output latency? I might tinker with the Pulse Audio driver and see if I can find an issue.

@EIREXE
>I've also done some testing on linux with pulse and it appears like the reported latency by get_output_latency is way too high (on the order of 50 ms) but it sure doesn't FEEL like it, I wonder what's going on.

I think I may have found part your problem.

From [this page](http://0pointer.de/lennart/projects/pulseaudio/doxygen/streams.html):
>If PA_STREAM_INTERPOLATE_TIMING is passed when connecting the stream, pa_stream_get_time() and pa_stream_get_latency() will try to interpolate the current playback time/latency by estimating the number of samples that have been played back by the hardware since the last regular timing update. It is espcially useful to combine this option with PA_STREAM_AUTO_TIMING_UPDATE, which will enable you to monitor the current playback time/latency very precisely and very frequently without requiring a network round trip every time.

PA_STREAM_INTERPOLATE_TIMING and PA_STREAM_AUTO_TIMING_UPDATE are passed in Godot's pulse driver so this applies. PA_STREAM_ADJUST_LATENCY is also passed allowing pulse to adjust the latency of the stream as it sees fit. This means means that `pa_stream_get_latency` may return different results each call, but in `AudioDriverPulseAudio` `pa_stream_get_latency` is called exactly once then that result is used for every subsequent `AudioDriverPulseAudio ::get_latency()` call (this appears to be for performance reasons). 

After realising this could be an issue I modified `AudioDriverPulseAudio::get_latency()` to not reuse the return value of `pa_stream_get_latency` and call it every time. Then I ran a project with this script:

```
extends Node

var latencies = []
var min_latency = null
var max_latency = null

func _process(_delta):
	var latency = AudioServer.get_output_latency()
	if min_latency == null or latency < min_latency:
		min_latency = latency
	if max_latency == null or latency > max_latency:
		max_latency = latency

func _exit_tree():
	print("AudioServer.get_output_latency() ranged between ", min_latency, " and ", max_latency)
````

And I got the following output:

````
AudioServer.get_output_latency() ranged between 0.014455 and 0.02272
````

When this was run the engine audio output latency was set to 5ms (256 audio frames).

So I guess in your case it's plausible that AudioDriverPulseAudio::get_latency() returned the correct latency at the time it was called, but Pulse eventually reduced it which is why it doesn't feel as high as Godot claims it is.

DISCLAIMER: I skimmed the Pulse Audio documentation extremely briefly.

With this merged we should probably make an issue/PR for the docs that mention the limitations of the audio latency project setting. Depending on the operating system and hardware audio driver Godot may have to pick the nearest latency that the system allows. Examples:

- Some drivers may have a limited range of buffer sizes they support, or a set of fixed values (e.g. my motherboard audio driver will allow buffer sizes of 128 to 4096 in increments of 32)
- Some hardware audio drivers may only support one latency (e.g. the Vive pro audio driver on my Windows 10 machine only allows a buffer size of 441 samples)
- Windows versions prior to 10 will only allow one latency. 

Should I go ahead and do this?

issue_context.title: No audio output latency option in project settings when using WASAPI
issue_context.body:
3.1.1 and 3.2

Although noted here: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/3.1/classes/class_projectsettings.html?highlight=latency#class-projectsettings-property-audio-output-latency
There is no option in the project settings to change the audio latency. 
Also, placing the option manually into the project.godot file allows the option to show up, but changing it does not change the audio output latency.

Here, the documentation talks about changing the size of audio buffers with the audio latency option in project settings : https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/audio/sync_with_audio.html
"Audio is mixed in chunks (not continuously), depending on the size of audio buffers used (check latency in project settings)."

-I know that this sync_with_audio documentation is specifically for 3.2, but even in 3.2 there is no audio latency option in project settings, and also does not effect latency. In fact, 3.2 does not output latency correctly at the moment; neither in debug monitor nor Performance.get_monitor(Performance.AUDIO_OUTPUT_LATENCY); it shows 0 constantly.

Is there actually way to change the buffer size/audio output latency?
comments:
On a newly-created project using 584ca0f156cec64c259382895e105cf27566a987, I see an **Audio -> Output Latency** setting in the Project Settings:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/61174907-190e4d80-a5a7-11e9-99e8-a737fd50ed39.png)
Hmmm, I am still not able to see that with a new project using 584ca0f15, downloaded from here: https://hugo.pro/projects/godot-builds/

It seems audio latency isn't configurable on all audio drivers. Due to how the setting is implemented, the project setting will only be visible if you're currently using an audio driver which supports tweaking the output latency:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/61175309-52e25280-a5ad-11e9-88a3-6743a3f1949f.png)

Most importantly, `drivers/wasapi` (the default audio driver on Windows) is missing from this list.

Oh ok thanks for clearing that up! I will look into changing my audio driver, but hopefully in the future it will be clear either in documentation or in the audio setting itself (maybe a greyed out option that explains why you can't change it). Do you know what drivers are able to change latency? Possibly is there a documented list for all operating systems? as I would like to change it for Android as well.

@JustYourAverageJosh See the screenshot I posted for the list of audio drivers that support adjusting the output latency. For the record, PulseAudio is the default audio driver on Linux, and CoreAudio is the audio driver used on macOS and iOS.

There's only one audio driver available on Android. On Windows, only WASAPI is available by default, but XAudio2 can be enabled by recompiling Godot with `xaudio2=yes` on the SCons command line. (I don't know if it's still working, as it doesn't get much testing.)

Looking at the WASAPI audio driver, it looks like we have no control on the size of the audio buffer/latency, which is likely why the setting isn't exposed.

Still, this should be changed to ensure that the setting is always defined, even if unused on WASAPI. Right now it makes it difficult to change audio latency from Windows for non-Windows exports, and the setting is removed from the docs when running `doctool` on Windows.

review_comments: [IAudioClient3](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/audioclient/nn-audioclient-iaudioclient3) is supported on Windows 10 only, interface won't be defined on older SDKs and MinGW and will fail to build.

Since the PR uses a feature exclusive to Windows 10 I tested on both Windows 10 and Windows 7 with the minimum requirements listed [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/development/compiling/compiling_for_windows.html) on fresh Windows installations in a virtual machine to ensure Godot could still run on older systems. For testing on Windows 7 I downloaded Visual Studio Community 2017 (v15.922) and installed it with the default settings which installed the Windows 10 SDK version 1809 (10.0.17763.0). IAudioClient3 is defined in the headers and compiles just fine, but will fail to initialise on Windows 7 (if this happens my PR falls back to IAudioClient at runtime). Is there documentation on the minimum required Windows SDK versions Godot should target?

I did not test with MinGW, as I didn't believe there to be a reason why that wouldn't work. Is it confirmed to not work with MinGW?

> Is there documentation on the minimum required Windows SDK versions Godot should target?

Godot aims to support Windows 7 and later. As for the Windows SDK version, I don't know exactly but we'd probably like Godot 4.0 to be buildable with Visual Studio 2017 and 2019 (2015 won't be a strict requirement by then).

When it comes to MinGW, we only care about modern MinGW-w64 setups (e.g. MSYS2), not the old MinGW32. We'd still like to keep MinGW support as it's used to cross-compile official Windows binaries.
